business.rationale:
Decision: keep the starting artifact unchanged (verbatim resubmission of the bound source).

Reasoning: the only evidence in the packet about the failure mode is an unverified probe contract whose feedback field is null — probe_feedback is absent, so the whitespace-normalization hypothesis is neither supported nor contradicted. No diagnostic observation says the emitted action strings are syntactically rejected; on inspection _fmt already emits canonical "(name arg1 arg2 ...)" with single spaces and no edge whitespace, so there is no positive evidence of a formatting defect to fix. The 0/8 development record is equally consistent with many causes (state-space blow-up under naive BFS on these instances, VAL/STRIPS-replay mismatch, or the empty-plan-on-frontier-exhaustion path), and the whitespace probe targets only the two public instances, not the eight development instances that dominate the objective.

Adding a term or parameter now would be an unevidenced change: the contract explicitly notes that evidence against deleting something does not license an addition, and nothing here licenses adding logic either. A speculative rewrite of a 0-parameter artifact risks introducing new failure modes (type/parameter-order errors, incorrect goal detection, non-deterministic ordering) without any measurement to justify it, and I have only one submission.

Uncertainty I cannot resolve: the actual rejection cause is unknown; I have no access to the evaluator's syntax or VAL output, so I cannot tell whether formatting, plan validity, or search completeness is at fault. Whatever the evaluator reports for this candidate is unknown to me now; I make no claim of success.
